claims.text: Conventional metal components such as steel are susceptible to rapid corrosion and erosion during continuous contact with high-temperature molten aluminum.
A 200–300 µm YSZ coating can be deposited on the metal components by thermal spraying.
Hot-dip aluminum plating components operate in prolonged contact with molten aluminum at temperatures above 660°C.
The thermally sprayed YSZ coating forms a ceramic barrier layer between molten aluminum and the metal substrate.
YSZ is chemically inert under the stated molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
YSZ is thermally stable at temperatures above 660°C.
The YSZ barrier prevents or reduces direct contact between molten aluminum and the metal substrate.
Reducing direct contact inhibits chemical reactions and alloying between molten aluminum and the substrate.
Inhibiting chemical reactions and alloying reduces corrosion and erosion of the components.
The thermal stability of YSZ allows the protective coating to remain effective under high-temperature operating conditions.
YSZ-coated components will exhibit significantly less corrosion and erosion than uncoated components under the same operating conditions.
Reduced corrosion and erosion will extend the service life of hot-dip aluminum plating components.
Uncoated components degrade rapidly because of chemical erosion and alloying with molten aluminum.
The protective effect depends on coating integrity, adhesion, and resistance to mechanical stresses.
Repeated thermal cycling may degrade the YSZ coating.
Interactions at the coating–substrate interface may affect coating performance.
